# Timescale Hierarchy — a Spectrum of Time Constants Generated by One Scalar Gradient on a Weighted Graph

**A bank of widely separated integration timescales does not have to be provisioned band by band. Scale the *recurrent excitatory gain* of every node by one scalar that increases along a structurally measured hierarchy, drop that gradient onto a directed, weighted, anatomically specific graph, and time constants spanning tens of milliseconds to seconds fall out of the coupling matrix's eigenvalues — with the slow modes spatially localised at the apex and the fast modes at the sensory periphery. Neither ingredient works alone: remove the gradient and the spread collapses; scramble the long-range weights while keeping the gradient and the hierarchy of timescales almost entirely disappears.**

> **Provenance.** Chaudhuri, Knoblauch, Gariel, Kennedy & Wang 2015, *A Large-Scale Circuit Mechanism for Hierarchical Dynamical Processing in the Primate Cortex*, Neuron 88(2):419–431, doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2015.09.008 (`raw/chaudhuri-2015-large-scale-circuit-hierarchical-dynamics.md`). A simulation study on the macaque tract-tracing connectome (Markov et al. 2014, core-nets.org): 29 injected cortical areas, all 812 possible directed pathways scored present/absent, 536 present (66% density), weights spanning **five orders of magnitude**. No new data; the contribution is the mechanism and its ablations.

---

## The construction, in three parts

| Part | Object | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Graph** | `FLN_ij` = fraction of labelled neurons — retrograde tracer count from area `j` to area `i`, normalised by total labelled neurons in the injection. Directed, weighted, complete presence/absence | Markov et al. 2014 |
| **Depth scalar** | `h_i` from **SLN** (fraction of a projection's source neurons in supragranular layers), fitted by a generalised linear model so that `h_i − h_j` predicts `SLN_ij` — the continuous hierarchy of [[wiki/concepts/canonical-cortical-microcircuit.md]] | Markov et al. 2014; Barone et al. 2000 |
| **Local heterogeneity** | Every excitatory input to area `i`, local **and** long-range, scaled by `(1 + η h_i)`, `η = 0.68`. Justified because basal dendritic **spine count** on layer-3 pyramidal cells rises sharply from primary sensory to prefrontal and correlates strongly with `h_i` | Elston 2000/2007 |

Each area is one threshold-linear excitatory/inhibitory pair — `τ_E = 20 ms`, `τ_I = 10 ms`, `w_EE = 24.3`, `w_IE = 12.2`, `w_EI = 19.7`, `w_II = 12.5 pA/Hz`, `β_E = 0.066`, `β_I = 0.351 Hz/pA` — with two *global* long-range gains `μ_EE = 33.7`, `μ_IE = 25.3 pA/Hz` that do not vary by edge. **All inter-areal specificity lives in `FLN_ij`; all inter-areal heterogeneity lives in the single scalar `η h_i`.** That is the entire parameterisation: one gradient, one graph, two global couplings. Conduction delays are mostly ignored (they appear only in a supplementary check).

**Why the whole thing is legible.** Threshold-linear areas make the network linear over its operating range, so activity is a weighted sum of eigenvectors of the coupling matrix, each decaying at its eigenvalue's rate. Timescales are not simulated and measured — they are the spectrum.

---

## The result: localised eigenvectors are the mechanism

Fast eigenvectors have their mass concentrated on sensory areas; slow eigenvectors have their mass concentrated on frontal areas (Chaudhuri, Bernacchia & Wang 2014, eLife 3:e01239, for the general result that gradients of a local property produce localisation).

`eigenvector localisation ⇒ separated timescales that are also separately addressable`

- If an eigenvector is small at node `k`, then whatever the input, that mode is weakly expressed at `k` — so the mode's time constant does not appear in `k`'s response.
- A pulse to V1 therefore propagates up with progressively slower decay: V1 and V4 transient, prefrontal traces persisting **seconds**; white-noise input gives the same ordering in autocorrelation decay.

This is the load-bearing transfer: **a timescale bank whose bands are also spatially separated modules, produced by one gradient rather than by `S` hand-chosen decay constants.** Nothing in the wiki's timescale machinery — [[wiki/entities/ms-ssm.md]]'s `S+2` stratified eigenvalue blocks, [[wiki/entities/s4.md]]'s common `Δ`, [[wiki/entities/simple-cycle-reservoir.md]]'s one-`λ`-per-block — generates its spectrum from a structural scalar, and none gets localisation for free.

---

## Ablations: what each ingredient is worth

| Manipulation | Effect on the spread of time constants | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Intact | Full range, tens of ms → seconds | — |
| **Remove the local gradient** (identical microcircuits, graph intact) | Range drastically reduced **and no relation to hierarchical position survives** | Long-range connectivity alone cannot produce the hierarchy |
| **Remove long-range feedback** | Range reduced | Slow areas form inter-areal excitatory loops with each other; part of the slowness is not local |
| **Remove all long-range projections**, stimulate each area alone | Range lower, and each area's time constant now *simply reflects its hierarchical position* | This is the **intrinsic** timescale — the local gradient read directly |
| **Scramble long-range edges**, gradient preserved | Hierarchy of timescales almost entirely removed | The gradient alone is insufficient |
| **Scramble long-range weights, preserve topology** | Separation strongly attenuated | **Weight specificity is required, not just wiring diagram.** A binarised connectome would not reproduce this |

**Hierarchical position is a weak predictor of the emergent timescale**: `r² = 0.25` (visual drive), `0.14` (somatosensory), `0.22` (rest). Two illustrative disagreements, both structural:

| Area | Hierarchy | Timescale | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **8m** (frontal eye field) | low | **slow** | Sits in the densely connected prefrontal/association core; its slowness is an inter-areal loop property and is strongly attenuated without feedback projections |
| **TEpd** | high | **fast** | Outside that core, strongly coupled to ventral-stream visual areas, so it inherits their speed |

---

## Timescale is input-dependent, not an area label

Stimulating primary somatosensory cortex (area 2) instead of V1 on the **same** anatomical network produces a **different** dynamical hierarchy: area 2 fastest, then F1 (primary motor), then area 5, parietal and premotor intermediate, prefrontal slow. Visual areas, now undriven, respond only through top-down projections and therefore express the *slow* distributed network state.

So an area's time constant is approximately determined by three quantities, only one of which is a property of the area:

`τ_i ≈ f( h_i , proximity to the slow association core , graph distance from the current input )`

**The prediction this makes, and the reconciliation it offers.** In the nonlinear extension, the timescale of *small fluctuations* around baseline reflects the isolated area's intrinsic properties, while *large* responses express time constants of the whole system. That is the wiki's threshold between "timescale as a fixed per-area property" and "timescale as a run-time network state" ([[wiki/empirical-tensions.md]] T319) — and it explains why hundreds-of-milliseconds spontaneous autocorrelations predict seconds-long sensitivity to stimulus structure.

---

## The nonlinear extension: the same gradient is a bifurcation parameter

Replacing the threshold-linear area with the Wong–Wang mean-field reduction of a spiking network (NMDA gating `s_N`, `τ_N = 60 ms`, `τ_I = 10 ms`, `γ = 0.641`, `w_EE = 250.2 pA`, `w_EI = 8.110 pA/Hz`, `w_IE = 303.9 pA`, `w_II = 12.5 pA/Hz`) and sweeping the same scaling `(1 + η h_i)`:

| Recurrent gain | Regime |
|---|---|
| Low (sensory end) | Single stable state — transient response only |
| High (association end) | **Bistable**: resting state + self-sustained persistent activity; integrates input over time and holds it after stimulus offset |

`one scalar gradient sweeps a bifurcation, so "fast relay" and "working-memory store" are the same circuit at two settings`

Consequences worth copying:
- The transition is continuous in the parameter, so a model does not have to *choose* which modules get a memory — the depth scalar allocates it.
- Long-range input can shift a local circuit across the boundary: an area with no persistent activity in isolation can hold activity under a weak long-range control signal. **A cheap, non-synaptic gate on whether a module is a store or a wire** ([[wiki/concepts/working-memory.md]], [[wiki/concepts/attractor-dynamics.md]]).
- Timescales of small perturbations around the low state (Jacobian eigenvalues) **predict** an area's capacity for the much longer timescales of large inputs — a probe that costs one small perturbation.

---

## The structure–function consequence: heterogeneity breaks the correlation everyone reports

| Model | `r²` between functional connectivity and anatomical connectivity |
|---|---|
| Homogeneous areas (standard assumption in whole-brain models) | **0.83** |
| With the gradient of local excitation | **0.53** |

The heterogeneous model is the more realistic one, and it *degrades* the structure–function correlation — which reframes the long-standing residual variance in that literature ([[wiki/concepts/effective-connectivity.md]], [[wiki/concepts/network-communication-models.md]]) as a **local-microcircuit signal rather than measurement noise**. Two further results in the same direction:

- **Lesion impact on the global correlation structure is predicted by an area's intrinsic time constant, not by its hierarchical position** (`r² = 0.18` for hierarchy alone). Slow frontal and temporal areas dominate.
- The strongest influencers combine *intermediate-to-high* hierarchical position with strong connections to other slow areas — STPc and PBr, not the apex. **Degree and depth both mispredict influence; the dynamical variable is the right one** ([[wiki/concepts/connectome-hubs-and-cores.md]], [[wiki/concepts/network-control-theory.md]]).

**(brainstorm) The transferable diagnostic.** For any trained modular model, estimate each module's autocorrelation time constant from small-noise perturbation at rest, then ablate modules and measure the change in the inter-module correlation matrix. If the biological ordering transfers, `τ` beats degree, centrality and layer index at predicting ablation impact — a one-forward-pass ranking of which modules a network actually depends on, and it is not run anywhere in the wiki.

---

## Relevance to a reasoning model

- **A timescale spectrum can be a consequence rather than a hyperparameter.** `G67` complains that nothing decides how many timescales a model needs or where the bands go. This is an existence proof that the question can be *dissolved*: parameterise one scalar field over modules (here `η h_i`, one number plus a structurally measured coordinate) and read the spectrum off the resulting operator. The bands are not chosen; they are eigenvalues.
- **Depth must be measured, and the graph must be weighted.** The gradient is placed along an SLN-derived hierarchy, and the result dies if edge *weights* are scrambled even with topology preserved. A model that types modules by layer index and couples them uniformly has thrown away both of the ingredients.
- **Reasoning needs the slow end and the fast end in one system, not one setting.** The same recurrent-gain axis that gives sensory areas transient responses gives association areas bistability and seconds-long integration; a uniform architecture must pick one, and picking the slow end costs responsiveness.
- **Slow modules are the intervention points.** If a model's global coordination is dominated by its slowest units, then control, gating and lesion-robustness analyses should be indexed by `τ` rather than by connectivity — and slow units are also the expensive ones to get wrong.
- **Attenuation is the unsolved cost.** Signals lose amplitude climbing the hierarchy in this model; the authors flag it and point to synchrony or stronger feedback as fixes. Any deep module stack built this way inherits the problem ([[wiki/concepts/inter-areal-synchrony.md]]).

---

## Open problems

| Problem | Why it is open |
|---|---|
| **Nothing learns the gradient** | `η` is one fitted global scalar and `h_i` comes from anatomy. There is no account of how a system would acquire its own depth scalar, which is exactly what `G67` asks for and what this construction assumes |
| **Cortico-cortical only** | No thalamus, no neuromodulation, no subcortical loops. The authors name thalamocortical projections as the likely gater of inter-areal interactions — i.e. the run-time control variable is precisely what is missing ([[wiki/concepts/transthalamic-context-routing.md]]) |
| **Timescales are never measured against these areas' timescales in the same animals** | The model's ordering agrees with Murray et al. 2014's seven areas, but there is no systematic measurement of area timescales *under different stimuli*, which is the paper's most distinctive prediction |
| **One scalar for two things** | Local and long-range excitation are scaled by the same `η h_i`, justified by a conserved local/long-range synapse ratio. If the two dissociate, the gradient becomes two gradients and the ablations do not disambiguate them |
| **Delays absent** | Conduction delay is the mechanism [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-hierarchy.md]] uses to explain the same phenomenon (hypomyelinated apex → long integration window). Here it is set aside, so the two accounts are never run against each other |
| **No laminar structure, no learning** | SLN is used to fit a hierarchy and then discarded; areas have no layers, and no plasticity shapes the gradient, the weights or the spectrum |

---

## Connections

- **[[wiki/concepts/canonical-cortical-microcircuit.md]]** — supplies the depth scalar this page's gradient is laid along: SLN% turns hierarchical position into a continuous, structurally measured coordinate, and this page is the demonstration that the coordinate is *load-bearing dynamically* — scaling recurrent gain by it produces the timescale spread, and the same coordinate correlates with layer-3 pyramidal spine count.
- **[[wiki/concepts/parallel-timescale-streams.md]]** — the measured phenomenon this page supplies a circuit for, and a disagreement about provisioning: that page finds six concurrent streams over one shared state codebook, this page generates a continuum of time constants from one gradient with no codebook at all, so the shared-alphabet property is unexplained by this mechanism.
- **[[wiki/concepts/broadcast-hierarchy.md]]** — the rival account of the same slow apex: that page derives long integration windows from hypomyelination, low neurite density and convergent input (conduction physics), this page derives them from a gradient of recurrent excitatory gain with delays explicitly omitted — two mechanisms for one observation, never run against each other ([[wiki/empirical-tensions.md]] T319).
- **[[wiki/concepts/neuronal-parameter-heterogeneity.md]]** — the same claim that heterogeneity is functional, with the opposite provisioning: HIFI learns a 5-vector per neuron on a bi-level loop, this page gets a functional spread from **one** scalar times a structural coordinate — and its Laplacian smoother over neighbouring units is a weak form of the gradient this page imposes outright.
- **[[wiki/concepts/effective-connectivity.md]]** — this page is a biophysical network model in that page's three-part template (threshold-linear or Wong–Wang neuronal model, no observation model, no inversion), and it supplies the reason the descriptive structure–function correlation is bounded: adding real local heterogeneity drops `r²` from 0.83 to 0.53, so the residual is microcircuit signal.
- **[[wiki/concepts/mean-field-reduction.md]]** — the rung this model occupies: rung 4 (neural mass, one E and one I number per area) for the linear results and the Wong–Wang reduction of a spiking network for the nonlinear ones, with the spectrum of the coupling matrix playing exactly the role that page's operator `Q` plays for a single ensemble.
- **[[wiki/concepts/connectome-hubs-and-cores.md]]** — a competing answer to "which nodes matter": that page's core is identified by six *graph* measures, this page finds lesion impact on global correlation structure predicted by an area's **intrinsic time constant**, with hierarchy alone at `r² = 0.18` and the top influencers (STPc, PBr) at intermediate depth.
- **[[wiki/concepts/network-control-theory.md]]** — the dynamical variable that page's controllability metrics omit: control energy is computed on a graph with identical nodes, and this page shows node heterogeneity dominates who moves the global state.
- **[[wiki/concepts/attractor-dynamics.md]]** — the bifurcation the depth scalar sweeps: increasing recurrent gain along the hierarchy carries an area from a single stable state into bistability (rest + persistent activity), so "relay" and "attractor store" are one circuit at two parameter settings, and a weak long-range input can move an area across the boundary at run time.
- **[[wiki/concepts/working-memory.md]]** — the capacity this gradient allocates: persistent activity appears only above a threshold in recurrent gain, so which modules can hold information is set by a structural coordinate rather than by design, and small-perturbation timescales predict which modules have the capacity before it is used.
- **[[wiki/concepts/network-communication-models.md]]** — the unmodelled variable in every routing-cost account: all of that page's communication models score paths on a graph of identical nodes, while here identical graphs with different node gains give entirely different global dynamics.
- **[[wiki/entities/ms-ssm.md]]** — the engineering counterpart of this page's spectrum: `S+2` dyadic bands with hand-partitioned eigenvalue intervals, provisioned per band and unlocalised in space, against a spectrum generated by one scalar gradient whose modes are also spatially separated modules.
- **[[wiki/entities/ventral-visual-stream.md]]** — the fast branch of this page's hierarchy, and the check on its coverage: the ~10-stage cascade that must finish in ~100 ms is exactly the regime where the timescale gradient must stay *short*, and TEpd's fast time constant despite high hierarchical position is this model's account of why.
- **[[wiki/concepts/inter-areal-synchrony.md]]** — the fix the authors name for this model's residual defect: activity attenuates as it climbs the hierarchy, and synchronous firing or stronger feedback is offered as the mechanism that would let signals propagate without amplitude loss.
- **[[wiki/concepts/transthalamic-context-routing.md]]** — the missing run-time gate: this model is cortico-cortical only, and the authors point to thalamocortical projections as the likely setter of network state and gater of inter-areal interaction — the control variable a fixed gradient cannot supply.
- **[[wiki/entities/cpc.md]]** — a timescale set by an objective rather than by anatomy: the number of steps the contrastive score predicts ahead decides how slow the learned features are, with an interior optimum (12 steps, 120 ms) rather than the monotone gradient this page's cortical data shows.
